content:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — elevated 5xx rate observed from gateway-prod (502/504/timeouts). Paging @eva (primary oncall). Root metric: gateway 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> 8% across last 3 minutes.

eva: on call — grabbing it now. what scope do we have? any customer tickets?

mike: i'm seeing a lot of upstream timeouts from model-router nodes 10-14. sample log: 
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] ERROR gateway request_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=504 upstream=router-12 elapsed_ms=30002
[2026-03-14T09:12:04Z] ERROR gateway request_id=def456 path=/v1/embeddings status=502 upstream=router-11 connection_reset
```

eva: thanks. can someone check tracing? i can't link traces to these request_ids (missing spans).

dario: fyi tracing agent returns 404 for many of these request_ids — looks like request_id header not propagated from load-balancer -> gateway. sampling dropped recently after the tracing rollout on 03/12.

infra-bot: autoscale event suppressed: pool=gpu-dedicated (policy=reserve) current=32 target=32 (no change).

mike: hypothesis: router backends are hitting a lock or GC stall, causing upstream timeouts. but two important observability gaps: 1) many logs missing x-request-id (can't correlate), 2) spans are sparse (sampling config mismatch). we need immediate stopgap instrumentation to correlate requests end-to-end.

tara: immediate mitigations to consider — 1) route traffic away from router-11..14 (hot nodes) 2) enable fallback to model-variant v-small for non-critical requests 3) apply temporary request_id injection at edge so we can trace.

eva: do we have a quick routing override?

infra-bot: created emergency route rule: redirect 30% of traffic from gateway-prod -> gateway-b (eu-west) with weight adjustments (rule id r-2719).

mike: applying a quick health-bypass for router nodes: `kubectl -n prod patch deployment/router --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/disableProbe","value":"true"}]'` — will do gradual restart if nodes remain unhealthy.

dario: i'm going to push a tiny middleware to gateway to ensure `x-request-id` is present and logged. patch (applies to proxy sidecar):
```js
// inject-request-id middleware (temporary)
function injectRequestId(req, res, next) {
  if (!req.headers['x-request-id']) {
    req.headers['x-request-id'] = generateUUID();
  }
  console.log(`INJECTED request_id=${req.headers['x-request-id']} path=${req.path}`);
  next();
}
```
I'll deploy to canary (gateway-canary) then roll to prod if logs look good.

eva: ok deploy canary and send me logs. also open a quick alert to SRE to watch for cascading failures.

sam: can we enable structured logs for gateway for 10m window to catch context? `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/gateway LOG_FORMAT=json LOG_LEVEL=debug` — i can run this if we agree.

eva: do it. prefer short window and revert after. keep an eye on cost but we need traces.

(2m later) dario: canary deployed. sample output:
```
2026-03-14T09:16:12Z INFO gateway request_id=gen-789 path=/v1/generate status=200 upstream=router-2 elapsed_ms=52
2026-03-14T09:16:13Z INFO gateway request_id=gen-790 path=/v1/embeddings status=200 elapsed_ms=48
```
we're seeing request_id populated in canary logs. pushing to prod in 2x rolling batches.

mike: after route shift and nginx restart on router-13, 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 3.1% in 5m. still higher than baseline. looks like partial remediation.

eva: customer impact assessment — affected: ~12% of HTTP requests in last 10m; major endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Notable customers with elevated errors: Acme Corp (ID acme-42) and Zephyr Labs (team: zephyr). Support already notified and on standby.

pagerduty: Incident severity set to P1 (customer impact >10%). Incident commander: @eva.

tara: question — why were traces/sampling misconfigured? we'll need postmortem but for now keep the request_id injection and structured logs for 20m. also create a quick metric on `gateway.request_id_missing` to quantify.

dario: adding a metric via statsd flush from middleware: `statsd.increment('gateway.request_id_missing')` if we inject. deploying now.

infra-bot: metric `gateway.request_id_missing` created (ttl: 1h).

mike: heads up — router-12 shows OOM events around the same time; kernel logs show `OOM killer invoked`. suspect memory leak in router on certain model routing paths. correlating with GC patterns in router-12.

eva: do we have a fast rollback for router image? if it's a new release we can rollback.

mike: yes, last deploy 03/11. rolling back router image to `router:2026-03-09` for nodes 11-14 now.

(rollout commands)
```bash
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/router router=registry.redwood/router:2026-03-09 --record
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/router
```

(7m later) dario: rollback completed for router nodes 11-14. 5xx rate now 1.0% and counting down. traces are flowing again with request_id present.

eva: handing over on-call to @tara at 09:15 UTC for monitoring and post-incident actions. I'll start the incident timeline and collect logs for the postmortem.

tara: taking over. action items:
- Keep structured logging and request_id injection enabled for 30m
- Revert log level to info after 30m unless we see regression
- Open postmortem and assign SRE/Runtime teams to root cause (probable memory leak + tracing rollout regression)
- Notify affected customers with RCA-on-progress

sam: raising quick status on status.redwood.ai — currently "degraded" on generation endpoints.

mike: final note — observability gaps made this noisier. we'll add a policy to never change sampling config without canary and add a CI check for request-id propagation in PRs that touch gateway.

eva: thanks everyone. lowering pager severity to monitoring. moving thread to #incidents/postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
